name: Saint Joseph
history: The husband of the Virgin Mary and foster father of Jesus, a just man of the house of David. The Gospels record no word of his, only his obedience: four times God spoke to him in dreams and four times he rose and did as he was told. Pius IX declared him Patron of the Universal Church in 1870.
life: Joseph was a craftsman of Nazareth, a tekton, which may mean a carpenter or a builder. Betrothed to Mary, he found she was with child and, being a just man, resolved to divorce her quietly, until an angel told him in a dream to take her as his wife. He took the family to Bethlehem for the census, fled with them by night into Egypt, and brought them home to Nazareth. With Mary he searched three days for the boy Jesus and found Him in the Temple. He is not mentioned again in the public ministry, and tradition holds that he died before it, in the arms of Jesus and Mary, which is why he is the patron of a happy death. Saint Teresa of Ávila spread devotion to him, Leo XIII wrote an encyclical on him, and John XXIII added his name to the Roman Canon.
prayerTo: Saint Joseph, guardian of the Redeemer and husband of Mary, you protected the Holy Family in silence and obedience. Protect my family and the whole Church. Teach me to work honestly, to listen for God’s voice and to act on it, and be with me at the hour of my death. Amen.
penance: This is a solemnity, so keep it as a feast even in Lent. In the Sicilian custom of Saint Joseph’s table, share a good meal with someone or give food to the poor.
meditation: Joseph says nothing in the Gospels. He rises and does what he is told. What has God already asked of you that you have not yet risen to do?
